Quick bottleneck size estimation (beta-binomial approximate MLE)

Source: R/bottleneck-quick.R
quickBottleneck.Rd

Estimates transmission bottleneck size using the approximate beta-binomial method of Sobel Leonard et al. (2017), which does not model sequencing depth explicitly. For the exact beta-binomial method (which accounts for finite read depth) or other approaches (presence-absence, KL divergence, Wright-Fisher), use the ViralBottleneck package (Zheng et al. 2025, Virus Evolution 11:veaf071) via asViralBottleneckInput.

Usage

quickBottleneck(whe, pairId, maxNb = 200L, threshold = 0.03)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with transmission pairs defined in colData.

pairId

Character. Which pair to estimate.

maxNb

Integer. Maximum bottleneck size to evaluate (default: 200); a single whole number of at least 1.

threshold

Numeric. Variant calling threshold (default: 0.03), a single number above 0 and below 0.5.

Value

A named list: Nb (MLE), ci (95% CI), loglik, n_variants, n_excluded, pair_id. n_excluded is a named integer, as from exactBottleneck, of the donor variants at or above threshold left out: recipient_failed_qc, sites where QC removed a recipient call at or above threshold, which is not an absence (see asViralBottleneckInput); unknown_depth, always 0 here, since this method does not use depths; and donor_near_fixation, donor variants above 1 - threshold.

Details

As in the published method, the donor variants used have frequencies from threshold to 1 - threshold; those above are left out, with a message, since a donor variant at frequency 1 that the recipient lacks has probability 0 under every Nb. The function stops with an error when the log-likelihood is not finite at any Nb of the grid, where it would otherwise return Nb = 1.

References

Sobel Leonard A et al. (2017). Transmission Bottleneck Size Estimation from Pathogen Deep-Sequencing Data, with an Application to Human Influenza A Virus. J Virol 91:e00171-17. doi:10.1128/JVI.00171-17

Examples

vcf1 <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
vcf2 <- system.file("extdata", "test_recipient.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(c(vcf1, vcf2),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("donor", "recipient"),
        role = c("donor", "recipient"),
        pair_id = c("p1", "p1")),
    caller = "ivar")
quickBottleneck(whe, pairId = "p1", maxNb = 50L)
#> $Nb
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $ci
#> [1] 1 7
#> 
#> $loglik
#> [1] -5.102543
#> 
#> $n_variants
#> [1] 15
#> 
#> $n_excluded
#> recipient_failed_qc       unknown_depth donor_near_fixation 
#>                   0                   0                   0 
#> 
#> $pair_id
#> [1] "p1"
#>
